<!-- pr-reviewer: aace33bb32d87565028da457c316076c1ae3a687 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- Every machine-name write in a `( )` or `;` post now goes through the post's own `clean()` with a `CAMCRAFT` fallback: fanuc, fanuc-lathe, haas, mazak (`onOpen`), sinumerik (`;` line), tormach (via `note`). I grepped all seven `.cps` files for comment writers. The other comment text (setup, op, tool) was already cleaned by `commentParam` since #257. The remaining raw `"(" + s + ")"` writes are the `msg()` fallbacks, which only run when the host has no `message()`.
- Heidenhain does not need the change: its name becomes the program name via `[^A-Za-z0-9._-]` to `_`, and its notes use `; ` with the `*` and `;` stripped by its own `clean()`.
- The Tormach active-comment guard only touches `note()`, whose callers all prefix their text (`SETUP:`, `OPERATION:`, `T<n> ...`). That leaves the machine name as the only text that can reach the keywords. The post's own probe line `(MSG, PROBE HIT ON POSITIONING)` (tormach.cps:420) is written with `block()` directly, so the guard cannot neuter it. The probe suites confirm this (`probe_guard`, `probe_op`, `inverted_probe`).
- The engine default `writeComment()` (js.rs) now strips parens and control characters. Nothing is changed beyond the stated scope.
- No golden changed: `git diff upstream/main` shows no `tests/golden` or snapshot files. The posts' output for the existing fixtures is byte-identical, since the fixtures' machine names hold no parens. I would not expect any shipped-machine golden to change, and none does.
- The test pins the shipped names: `every_bundled_machine_name_posts_a_single_header_comment` walks every Tormach `.mch` (asserts at least 10), including the `(ML)`, `(Series I)` and `(Series 3)` models. It also asserts a single balanced header comment starting with `(Tormach `. The hostile-name tests cover every mill dialect and the lathe.
- The decision record is in `docs/decisions/594-comment-escape.md`. The body ends `Fixes #594` and has a `Changelog:` line. The new module carries its provenance line.

**Local results** (trial merge with `upstream/main`: already up to date, no conflicts; own target dir)

|---|---|
| `comment_escape` | 3/3 pass |
| `camcraft-post` | all pass (3, 9, 3, 33 across its binaries) |
| `conformance` | 6 pass |
| `golden_cl` | 23 pass |
| `posting` | 17 pass |
| `tormach_post` | 10 pass |
| `tormach_machines` | 5 pass |
| `tormach_safe_retract` | 4 pass |
| `program_comments` | 4 pass |
| `fanuc_post` | 11 pass |
| `lathe_post` | 7 pass |
| `inverted_post` | 15 pass |
| `probe_guard` | 5 pass |
| `probe_op` | 11 pass |
| `heidenhain_block_form` | 4 pass |
| `sinumerik_safe_retract` | 3 pass |

| `setup_mounts_post` | 5 pass |
| `clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- `msg()` in tormach.cps:69 (and the same fallback in the other posts) still writes `"(" + s + ")"` unescaped when the host offers no `message()`. It is unreachable under the app, but it would nest on a name like `770MX (ML)` (see the `machine.name` in the tapping message at tormach.cps:451). Routing it through `clean()` or `note()` would close the gap.
- The `ACTIVE` guard is anchored at the start of the comment text, which is where LinuxCNC reads the keyword. A future `note()` caller that puts user text first would be guarded; one that prefixes it is already safe.
- Project and tool library names that reach a header would be covered the same way; I found none beyond the machine name.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
